fig01_score_time_clusters: Source-study pipeline reproduced on PISA 2025 Form A (n = 5591). (a) Score–time density with the four K-means centroids. (b) Silhouette by k; the shaded band is the conventional 'weak structure' range. (c) Silhouette of K-means (k = 4) on 100 datasets with the same marginals and rank correlation but no clusters (Gaussian copula), against the observed value.
fig02_04_items_icc: Homogeneous 2PL (M0) fitted on the training split: (a) item parameters; (b) phi correlations between items (pairwise complete); (c) item characteristic curves.
fig05_model_comparison: Training-split BIC differences. Blue: continuous-ability models; orange: models with class-specific item difficulties; grey: unrestricted LCA.
fig07_10_class_profiles_stability: Two-class mixture 2PL with class-specific difficulties (M1_2), training split. (a) Class difference in item difficulty after ability adjustment, with 95% bootstrap ranges (20 refits). (b) Adjusted Rand index of bootstrap assignments against the full-sample solution. (c) Correlation of the difference profiles across refits.
fig06_09_within_score: Within-score analysis (training split). (a) Certainty of class assignment. (b) Spread of the class posterior among students with the same score, observed vs a dataset simulated from the continuous 2PL with the same items and missingness. (c) Share of aberrant response patterns (l_z < −1.96).
fig11_null_simulation: Null simulations with no latent classes. Data are generated from the continuous model fitted to Form A, using either the fitted ability distribution or a skewed one, and the same N, items, missingness and duration model. Positive ΔBIC means the class model is preferred. Vertical lines mark the observed PISA values.
fig12_14_ablation_calibration: Held-out evaluation on the test split (30% of students). Masked items (30% of positions, 5 mask sets) are predicted from the unmasked responses. Models with '_time' also use the time spent on unmasked items. (a) Paired differences in log loss with student-bootstrap 95% CIs; the dashed line marks the pre-registered practical threshold (0.001 nats/item). (b) Reliability diagram for the first mask set.
fig13_dif: Differential item functioning on Form A (all students) by group membership. The dashed line is the Jodoin–Gierl threshold for moderate DIF.
